The file does not exhibit any of the red flags typically associated with supply chain attacks, such as unexpected network requests, obfuscated code, or unauthorized file operations that could exfiltrate data or execute malicious payloads during the sourcing phase.

The PKGBUILD is a clean, minimal packaging file with no evidence of malicious behavior. The source is fetched over HTTPS from the package's own upstream GitHub repository (github.com/dani-77/quickshell-d77) with a pinned SHA-256 checksum, which is actually better than SKIP. Dependencies are standard system packages (quickshell, power-profiles-daemon, alsa-utils, brightnessctl, etc.) and makedepends includes only rsync. The package() function performs only routine operations: running `make install` into $pkgdir and installing LICENSE/README.md to standard documentation directories. There are no network requests beyond the declared source, no obfuscated code, no eval/base64/curl/wget misuse, no file operations outside the package scope, and no signs of data exfiltration, backdoors, or tampering with unrelated system files.
